title: Sticky Toffee Pudding

source.book: The Cookie That Changed My Life
source.author: Nancy Silverton

ingredients.name: walnut halves
ingredients.notes: originally ¼ cup; toasted before adding to batter

ingredients.name: Medjool dates
ingredients.notes: about 15 dates; poached in tea, then pitted and chopped

ingredients.name: black tea leaves
ingredients.notes: or 1 tea bag, English breakfast or other black tea; used to poach the dates

ingredients.name: dark muscovado sugar
ingredients.notes: originally ¼ cup packed; or dark brown sugar; for the cake

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.notes: originally 1 teaspoon; Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for the cake

ingredients.name: dark muscovado sugar
ingredients.notes: originally 1½ cups packed; or dark brown sugar; for the sauce

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.notes: originally ¾ cup plus 2 tablespoons; for the sauce

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: originally 1 stick plus 3 tablespoons; cold, cubed; for the sauce

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.notes: originally ¼ teaspoon; Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for the sauce

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.notes: originally 1½ cups; for the whipped cream

ingredients.name: crème fraîche
ingredients.notes: originally ½ cup; or 122 g/½ cup sour cream

steps: Adjust an oven rack to the center position and preheat the oven to 325°F.

Spread the walnuts on a baking sheet and toast on the center rack until lightly browned and fragrant, 8 to 10 minutes, shaking the pan and rotating it front to back halfway through. Cool, then coarsely chop.
Increase the oven temperature to 350°F.
Coat the Bundt pan with cooking spray.

Make 1 cup of strong black tea and discard the tea bag or leaves. Pour the tea into a small heatproof bowl, add the dates, and soak until the tea cools to room temperature or for at least 15 minutes. Remove the dates (reserving the tea), then discard the pits and chop the dates.
Whisk the eggs and vanilla together in a small bowl. Sift the flour into a large bowl.

Beat the butter in a stand mixer fitted with the paddle on medium speed until soft but still cold, 3 to 4 minutes, scraping down the bowl as needed. Add the muscovado sugar, granulated sugar, and molasses and beat on medium speed until lightened in color, 3 to 4 minutes. Add the baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and cloves and beat on low speed about 15 seconds. With the mixer on low, drizzle in the egg/vanilla mixture, stopping to scrape down the bowl before each addition. Scrape down the bowl and paddle, then add the flour and mix on low until very little flour is visible, about 15 seconds. Add the toasted walnuts and mix on low about 15 seconds. Remove the bowl and paddle and clean with a spatula. Add the dates and their poaching tea and stir with a rubber spatula to combine, scraping the bottom of the bowl. (The batter will look broken — that's normal.)
Scrape the batter into the prepared Bundt pan and smooth the top with an offset spatula.
Bake on the center rack until the cake begins to pull away from the sides of the pan, springs back when touched, and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 40 to 50 minutes.

While the cake bakes, make the sauce: combine the muscovado sugar, cream, butter, molasses, and salt in a medium saucepan and heat over low heat, stirring with a silicone spatula until the butter melts. Remove from heat and stir in the whiskey.
Remove the cake from the oven. Poke holes in the cake with a skewer or toothpick, spaced about 1 inch apart. Spoon ¼ cup of the sauce over the cake and let sit 15 minutes to absorb.

Meanwhile, make the whipped cream: whip the cream in a stand mixer fitted with the whisk on low speed for about 1 minute until thickened enough not to spatter, then on medium-high until soft peaks form, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the crème fraîche and whip on medium-low until medium peaks form, about 1 minute.
Invert the cake onto a plate and drizzle ¼ cup of the remaining sauce over the top. Serve with the whipped cream and remaining sauce on the side.
notes: Three components: cake, toffee sauce, and whipped cream (yields one 6-inch Bundt cake). Headnote mentions the original Chi Spacca version is topped with vanilla ice cream and candied pecans instead of whipped cream.

title: WHOLE-WHEAT DATE-NUT BREAD
steps: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 350 degrees. Grease 8½ by 4½-inch loaf pan. Combine dates, boiling water, and baking soda in medium bowl, cover, and let sit until dates have softened, about 30 minutes.

make batter ​ Whisk whole-wheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt together in large bowl. Whisk buttermilk, sugar, oil, and egg in second bowl until smooth, then stir in dates and their soaking liquid until combined. Using rubber spatula, gently fold buttermilk mixture into flour mixture until just combined. Gently fold in walnuts. Transfer batter to prepared pan and smooth top.

bake ​ Bake until golden and skewer inserted in center comes out clean, 55 minutes to 1 hour, rotating pan halfway through baking. Let bread cool in pan on wire rack for 10 minutes. Remove bread from pan and let cool completely on wire rack, about 2 hours. Serve.
notes: The test kitchen’s preferred loaf pan measures 8½ by 4½ inches; if you use a 9 by 5-inch loaf pan, start checking for doneness 5 minutes earlier than advised in the recipe.

title: Sourdough Bagels
steps: Mix the sourdough starter at least 12 hours before planning to make the dough by combining 118g water, 25g mother starter, and 120g bread flour in a 1-quart container; cover and set in a warm place (75°F).
To mix the dough, place 355g water in a stand mixer bowl, sprinkle with yeast, and let rest for 5 minutes before whisking.
Add 263g of the matured sourdough starter, barley malt syrup, salt, and sugar to the water and whisk until homogeneous.
Add the high-gluten bread flour and mix with the dough hook on low speed for 2 minutes.
Divide the stiff dough into portions and develop the gluten using a food processor in 30-second increments with rests in between to avoid overheating.
Divide the dough into 11 pieces weighing 130 grams each.
Shape each piece into a log by folding the top edge toward the middle and pinching, repeating until a cylinder forms, then roll back and forth to 10 inches long.
Form a ring by wrapping the log around your palm, overlapping ends by 2 inches, and rolling the seam against the work surface to seal.
Place shaped bagels on greased, parchment-lined sheets; cover with greased plastic wrap and proof at room temperature for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 8 hours (or overnight).
Preheat the oven to 400°F and bring a 5-quart pot of water to a boil.
Perform a float test by placing a bagel in a bowl of water; it is ready to boil if it floats immediately to the surface.
Boil bagels in batches for 1 minute on the first side, then flip and boil for 30 to 60 seconds more.
Transfer boiled bagels back to the baking sheets and bake for 28 to 33 minutes, rotating sheets and switching racks halfway through, until lightly browned and they sound hollow when tapped.
Cool the bagels on their baking sheets.

title: LINGUINE sea urchin, chili
steps: Put the sea urchin tongues in a blender with a couple of splashes of olive oil, and blend it for a few seconds until it's a smooth puree with the consistency of melted ice cream. Put the mixture in the refrigerator.
Put a pot of heavily salted water on to boil, and put three or four shallow bowls for serving in a 200°F oven to warm.

When the water is boiling, add the pasta to it. At the same time, coat a large sauté pan with olive oil. Set the pan over medium heat and add the garlic. Let the garlic color, and when the pasta is just about al dente, remove the garlic from the sauté pan and discard it, and take the sea urchin mixture out of the refrigerator.
Transfer the pasta from the pot to the sauté pan with tongs, and lower the heat. Add a splash of pasta water to the pan and give the pan a shake. Add a generous pinch of chili flakes.

Remove the pan from the heat and add another splash of pasta water and the sea urchin mixture, tossing it gently with the pasta and putting the pan back on the heat for a couple of seconds and then removing it again. You don't want to cook the sea urchin at all—much the way you don't want to cook the eggs when you're making a carbonara. You want the sauce to have a creamy consistency; if it doesn't, add a little more pasta water. When the pasta is well coated with the sauce, transfer it to the warmed shallow bowls. Sprinkle a little sea salt over each bowl and serve.

title: "FISH AND CHIPS" Ale-Battered Blowfish with Malt Vinegar Jam

ingredients.name: blowfish tails
ingredients.notes: cleaned, 2 to 3 ounces (55 to 85 grams) each

steps: To make the malt vinegar jam: Lightly toast the caraway seeds in a small sauté pan over medium-low heat until fragrant, continuously swirling the pan to ensure even toasting. Let cool, then grind in a spice grinder until cracked but not ground to dust.
In a 1-quart saucepot, bring the vinegar, water, brown sugar, and fleur de sel to a boil over medium heat.

Whisk in the agar-agar and boil gently, whisking continuously, for 1 minute to activate the agar-agar. Transfer to a bowl and nestle in an ice-water bath. Chill, undisturbed, until the jam base is completely firm and set.
To make the split pea and ale batter: Grind the dried split peas to a fine powder in a spice grinder.
Transfer the pea powder to a bowl, add the Cup4Cup flour and salt, and mix thoroughly.
Whisk the ale into the dry mixture. If the batter is too thick, thin it with a bit more ale. The batter can be held at room temperature for up to 1 hour.
Fill a disposable piping bag with the set malt vinegar jam and pipe it into a small squeeze bottle.
To complete: Prepare the blowfish for frying by dusting each tail with all-purpose flour and dipping it into the batter to coat. Deep-fry in canola oil until golden and crisp.
Arrange the fried blowfish on serving plates and sprinkle with the crushed freeze-dried peas. Garnish the plate with beads of the malt vinegar jam, blanched fresh peas, and mint.

title: Ginger Scones

source.book: Nancy Silverton's Pastries from the La Brea Bakery
source.author: Nancy Silverton

ingredients.name: unbleached pastry flour
ingredients.notes: 2.25 cups unbleached pastry flour or unbleached all-purpose flour

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: 1.5 sticks, cut into 1-inch cubes and frozen

ingredients.name: candied ginger
ingredients.notes: finely chopped into 0.25-inch pieces to equal 0.67 cup

steps: Adjust the oven rack to the middle position and preheat the oven to 400°F.

In the bowl of a food processor fitted with the steel blade or in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, combine the flour, sugar, and baking powder. Pulse or mix on low to incorporate.
Add the lemon zest and butter. Pulse on and off, or mix on low, until the mixture is pale yellow and has the consistency of a fine meal.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and stir in the ginger.
Make a well in the center and pour in 0.5 cup of heavy cream.
Using one hand, draw in the dry ingredients, mixing until just combined. If the mixture feels dry, add a few more tablespoons of buttermilk (heavy cream).
Wash and dry your hands and dust them with flour.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured work surface and gently knead a few times to gather it into a ball.
Roll or pat the dough into a circle about 0.75 inch thick.
Cut out circles using a 3-inch round cutter, cutting as closely together as possible and keeping the trimmings intact.
Gather the scraps, pat and press the pieces back together, and cut out the remaining dough.
Place the circles 1 inch apart on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Brush the tops with the remaining cream.
Bake for 12 to 16 minutes, until the surface cracks and the scones are slightly browned.

title: Guinness Stout Ginger Cake
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 9 × 5-inch loaf pan, line the bottom and sides with parchment, and grease the parchment. Alternatively, butter and flour a 6-cup Bundt pan.
In a large saucepan over high heat, combine the stout and molasses and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat and add the baking soda. Allow to sit until the foam dissipates.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, whisk together the eggs and both sugars. Whisk in the oil.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, ground ginger, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and cardamom.
Combine the stout mixture with the egg mixture, then whisk this liquid into the flour mixture, half at a time. Add the fresh ginger and stir to combine.

Pour the batter into the loaf pan and bake for 1 hour, or until the top springs back when gently pressed. Do not open the oven until the gingerbread is almost done or the center may fall slightly. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.

title: Viennese Cream Brioche

source.book: Nancy Silverton's Pastries from the La Brea Bakery
source.author: Nancy Silverton

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: chilled and cut into 12 square pats

ingredients.name: crème fraîche
ingredients.notes: originally 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons; or sour cream

steps: Separate the dough into twelve 3-ounce pieces.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll the dough into 2-inch balls.
Flatten the balls into 5-inch discs, about ¼ inch thick.
Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and set aside in a warm place to proof, about 1 hour, until spongy to the touch.
Flip the discs over and allow them to finish rising, about 1 more hour.
Adjust the oven rack to the lower position and preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
Press a pat of butter into the center of each disc.
Brush around the rim with the beaten egg and sprinkle 1 teaspoon of the crystallized sugar around the edge.
Spoon about 3 tablespoons of crème fraîche over the butter in a mound, and sprinkle 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar over it.
Place 2 inches apart on the parchment-lined baking sheet and bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until lightly browned and the center is set.

title: Apple Cider Sticky Buns

source.book: Pastry Love: A Baker's Journal of Favorite
source.author: Joanne Chang

ingredients.name: Master Brioche Dough
ingredients.notes: originally 21 ounces / 600 grams; can substitute 2/3 recipe Whole Wheat Brioche dough

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apples
ingredients.notes: peeled, cored, and chopped into 1/2-inch pieces (about 2 1/3 cups)

steps: Mix the brioche dough and let it proof for 6 hours or up to overnight in the fridge as directed.
In a small saucepan, heat the apple cider, orange zest, cloves, ginger, nutmeg, and allspice to just under a boil.
Simmer the cider mixture for about 10 minutes until it reduces to approximately 1/2 cup.
Turn off the heat and add the chopped apples to the reduced cider; allow to cool to room temperature.
Set a sieve over a bowl and drain the apples, reserving the apples and cider reduction separately.
In a medium saucepan, combine the butter and 1 1/4 cups (275 grams) of the brown sugar; heat over medium-high heat until the sugar melts and starts to boil (about 3 minutes).
Whisk in the reserved cider reduction, honey, cream, and salt until thoroughly combined to create the sticky goo.
Remove the apple cider goo from the heat and allow it to cool to room temperature.
On a floured work surface, roll out the chilled brioche dough into a 12 x 12-inch square.
In a small bowl, stir together the remaining 1/4 cup (55 grams) brown sugar, superfine sugar, and cinnamon.
Sprinkle the cinnamon sugar mixture evenly over the surface of the dough square and scatter the apples on top.
Roll up the dough and slice into 8 individual buns.
Pour the cooled apple cider goo into a 9 x 13-inch baking pan and arrange the buns cut side down, evenly spaced.
Cover the pan with plastic wrap and proof at warm room temperature for about 2 hours until the dough is puffy and the buns are touching.
Preheat the oven to 350°F and bake the buns for 30 to 40 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until golden brown.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool in the pan for 20 to 30 minutes.
Invert the buns onto a serving platter and spoon any extra goo remaining in the pan on top.

title: Salted Vanilla Shortbread

ingredients.name: vanilla pod
ingredients.notes: fat, scraped; or 5–10g / 1–2 tsp good quality vanilla bean paste

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.notes: ¾ cup; depending on brand, you might need more or less

steps: For the shortbread, cream the butter with the sugar. You want it to be light but not ultra-fluffy or white—1 minute should do it.
Mix the dry ingredients together, then stir them into the butter mixture with the vanilla until no dry bits remain.
Roll into an approximately 3-inch wide log and wrap.
Chill the dough in the freezer/fridge so you can cut it neatly. Around 2 hours in the fridge or 30–40 minutes in the freezer.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Slice the chilled log into ½-inch rounds and place on two large baking sheets.
Bake for 15–17 minutes, then let cool completely on a cooling rack.

To glaze, mix together the grapefruit zest and juice and the powdered sugar—the glaze should be thick but still run off the spoon, like thick honey. You may need to add a little more sugar/juice to get it just right.
Spoon over the cooled shortbread rounds.
Let rest for 20–30 minutes to harden.

title: Almond Croissants 2.0
steps: To make the syrup, heat the ingredients together in a pan, then allow to cool and infuse for at least 30 minutes. Can be made up to 30 days in advance and kept in the fridge. [1]
Preheat the oven to 400°F. [1]
Tear the croissants up into 2–3¼-inch pieces. They can be different sizes and shapes—a mixture of middle bits and crust is good. Put the frangipane into a piping bag. [1]

Soak the croissant pieces in the syrup, then alternate into the molds with frangipane until they are about 90% full. You should have 30–45g/1–1½ oz frangipane per mold and 40–55g/1½–2 oz syrup-soaked croissants. [2]
Place the molds on a baking sheet, place a piece of parchment paper on top, then weigh down with a baking sheet on top. [2]

Bake for 30 minutes. Let cool slightly in the molds, about 10 minutes, then turn out onto a cooling rack to cool completely. If desired, you can return them to the oven to brown the other edges for about 10 minutes at the same temperature. Once you are happy with the color, move to a rack to cool completely. [2]
Dust with powdered sugar before serving. The croissants will keep in an airtight container for 2–3 days at room temperature but the powdered sugar will need to be reapplied. [3]

title: 3-DAY FOCACCIA

ingredients.name: bread flour
ingredients.notes: originally ¾ cup plus 2 Tbsp; for poolish

ingredients.name: bread flour
ingredients.notes: originally 4⅓ cups; for dough part I

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.notes: originally 1½ cups plus 2 Tbsp; for dough part I

ingredients.name: dry yeast
ingredients.notes: originally ⅔ tsp; for dough part I

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.notes: originally 2½ tsp; for dough part II

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.notes: originally 3 Tbsp; for dough part II

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.notes: originally 100–150g (½–⅔ cup); for dough part II

steps: Day 1: Mix the flour, yeast, and water together to make a poolish. Cover and let the poolish rest for 12 hours.
After 12 hours, it should be bubbly and ripe, aka ready to use. You can check it’s well aerated by seeing if it floats in water.
Day 2: Mix the poolish, flour, water, and yeast together until it forms a rough dough. It will look shaggy and ugly. Cover and allow to autolyse for 30 minutes.

Dissolve the salt in the water and then mix this into the dough—squeeze it in with your hands until combined. Rest for 30 minutes, keeping it covered. Now add 1–2 tablespoons of the olive oil, coat your hands and stretch and fold the dough—pick the dough up from the middle, stretching it, then folding it over itself gently. Repeat this four or five times, until smooth. Cover and let rest for 1 hour.
Add 1–2 tablespoons of olive oil and stretch and fold the dough—it should be quite puffy at this stage. I call it a puppy’s belly!
Cover and let rest for 1 hour—it should be getting puffy and big each time you leave it.
Check the gluten development. It should be stronger but may not be fully developed (e.g., the dough tears). If needed, add more olive oil and stretch the dough.

After 30 minutes, check the gluten development again—you should be able to make a thin stretchy windowpane. If it is well developed, you can move it into an oiled bowl and put into the fridge. Keep it covered so it doesn’t dry out.
After 1 hour, check and de-gas the dough by pressing it down. If it is bubbling up too much in the fridge (it probably will), check later to see it’s in check.
Cover and chill for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight.

Make the slow-roast tomatoes: Preheat the oven to 325°F. Cut the cherry tomatoes in half, toss with the olive oil, and lay on a baking sheet. Season with salt and black pepper. Bake for 1 hour or until wrinkled but not colored. Cool, then move into a container and keep in the fridge.

Day 3: With oiled hands, move the dough onto an oiled baking sheet, balling it in your hands slightly to help give it a smooth surface. Spread the dough out slightly, then cover with olive oil so it doesn’t form a crust. Let rest for 1–1½ hours, until it relaxes.

Oil your hands, then dimple the top of the dough and redistribute the air bubbles. You can also lift up the edges and sides of the focaccia, which can help reveal hidden side bubbles! Let rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 475°F.

Dimple the dough again and press the roasted cherry tomatoes into the dough. Remember to poke them quite deep into the dough. Toss sprigs of rosemary with a little olive oil so they are lightly covered then press into the dough, followed by a little flaky salt.
Bake for 10 minutes, then turn the oven down to 425°F and bake for 10–15 minutes, until golden. Remove from the sheet and cool on a rack.

title: Walnut-Date Bars (Food for the Gods)

ingredients.name: medjool dates
ingredients.notes: pitted and cut into 1/2-inch pieces; originally 4 cups (about 26)

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: pliable but still cold; originally 2 cups

steps: Preheat the oven to 325°F. Line a 13 x 18-inch baking sheet with parchment paper, coat the parchment with cooking spray, and set aside.
Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt into a bowl and set aside.
Cut the dates into 1/2-inch pieces. Put a generous 60g / 1/2 cup of the flour mixture into a bowl and dredge the dates in it. Set aside.
Cream the butter and both sugars in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment on medium speed until just incorporated.
Add the eggs one at a time, continuing to mix on medium speed, beating well after each addition to fully incorporate before adding the next.
Add the rest of the flour mixture and the dates and mix just until incorporated—but no longer.
Add the walnuts and mix just until incorporated, about 20 seconds.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared pan.
Bake until a cake tester inserted into the center of the bars comes out clean, about 27 minutes, rotating the baking pan after 13 minutes to ensure even baking.
Cool in the pan until completely cool. Cut into 3 x 3-inch squares.

title: Food for the Gods Molasses, Date, and Walnut Squares

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: softened at room temperature (115 g), plus 1 tbsp to grease the pan

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: 95 g, plus 2 tsp to dust the pan

ingredients.name: dates
ingredients.notes: pitted and cut into 1/2-inch (12 mm) dice (145 g)

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and put a rack in the middle position.
Grease the bottom and sides of an 8 by 8-inch (20 by 20 cm) square baking dish with 1 tablespoon butter. Dust with the 2 teaspoons flour, tapping the pan so the flour sticks to the butter.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine the remaining 3/4 cup (95 g) flour, the baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Whisk to sift and combine these dry ingredients, getting rid of any lumps.
In a large mixing bowl, cream the softened butter and brown sugar together with a whisk.
Add the eggs and molasses, whisking to meld.
Switch to a rubber spatula and mix in the dates, walnuts, and breadcrumbs.
Add the flour mixture to the batter and fold to combine.
Pour the batter into the greased and floured baking dish and flatten with the spatula into an even layer.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes on the middle rack until a toothpick or skewer comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and let cool on the countertop. Cut into 2-inch (5 cm) squares and serve.

title: Coconut Milk Chicken Adobo

source.book: Filipinx: Heritage Recipes from the Diaspora
source.author: Angela Dimayuga

steps: In a large pot, heat the coconut oil on medium until shimmering. Add the whole peppercorns, coarsely cracked black pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Lay the drumsticks and thighs in the pan, skin side down, and raise the heat to medium high. Cook for about 5 minutes undisturbed, until the fat starts to render and the skin turns slightly brown.
Using kitchen tweezers or tongs, flip over the chicken.
Add the garlic, coconut milk, vinegar, soy sauce, bay leaves, serrano chile, and 1 cup (240 ml) water. Let the mixture come to a boil.
Put a lid on the pot, reduce the heat to medium low, and simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally. The chicken should feel loose, almost ready to slip off the bone.
Remove the lid, raise the temperature to medium high, and reduce the sauce by cooking uncovered for another 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick as velvet.
Serve over rice to soak up the sauce.

title: Banana Bread
steps: Preheat the oven to 350ºF. Lightly grease a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan.
Mix together the flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a large bowl.
In another bowl, mix together the mashed banana, sugar, sour cream, olive oil, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the bowl with the flour mixture.
Gently mix everything together—sprinkle in the chopped bananas while mixing and mix until just combined.
Pour the batter into the loaf pan and sprinkle with a little turbinado sugar.
Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean or with some moist crumbs.
Let cool a little before slicing.

To serve, heat a small skillet over medium-high heat. Add a tiny bit of grapeseed oil. Griddle the bread on both sides until golden brown and warmed all the way through. Top with a scoop of coconut sorbet and drizzle with chocolate–olive oil sauce.

title: Chocolate--Olive Oil Sauce
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bowl set over a pan of simmering water.
Slowly stream in the olive oil while whisking constantly.
Season aggressively with salt.
Use immediately or, if it cools and hardens, just warm it up to bring it back to liquid.

title: Creamy Cashew Dip with Jalapeño and Seedy Seaweed Crackers

ingredients.name: jalapeno oil
ingredients.notes: 3 tbsp total; 2 tbsp blended into dip, 1 tbsp for drizzling

ingredients.name: mixed fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: small handful, like small dill and parsley sprigs and oregano leaves

steps: Preheat the oven to 300ºF.
Stack the nori sheets shiny-side down. Use kitchen scissors to cut along the indentations into long strips. Stack those strips and snip them crosswise into ½-inch-wide strips.

Combine the nori, chia seeds, flax seeds, sunflower seeds, scallions, garlic, chile flakes, and 0.75 cup water in a medium mixing bowl. Stir well and let the mixture sit for about 3 minutes so the chia has time to fully bloom.
Spread the chia mixture between two 17 × 12-inch sheets of parchment paper into a thin (about ⅛-inch), even layer using a rolling pin or round bottle.
Transfer the layers to a large sheet pan and slowly peel off the top parchment sheet.
Sprinkle with the flaky salt and bake for about 45 minutes until crispy. If needed, flip and cook for 10 minutes more.
Let the cracker cool, then break it into pieces.
Soak the cashews in 1.5 cups of water in a narrow jar for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, combine the shallot and kosher salt in a small bowl; let sit for 10 minutes, then stir in the vinegar.
Transfer the cashews and soaking water to a blender with the shallot mixture and 2 tablespoons of the jalapeño oil. Puree on high until smooth, about 2 minutes.
Transfer the dip to a bowl and drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon of jalapeño oil. Serve with the crackers and herbs.

title: Jalapeño Oil
steps: Combine the oil, chiles, and salt in a medium saucepan, set it over medium-high heat, and wait until bubbles form around the chiles.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and let the chiles sizzle just until they turn a brighter shade of green, about 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the mixture cool.
Transfer to a blender, making sure to scrape any salt that has collected in the bottom of the pan into the blender as well. Puree until as smooth as possible, about 1 minute.

title: TOSTADAS DE ATÚN O TRUCHA

ingredients.name: leek
ingredients.notes: thick, white part only, sliced into 1/8-inch / 3mm-thick rounds

ingredients.name: rice bran oil
ingredients.notes: or safflower oil, or any vegetable oil with a high smoke point (480ml)

ingredients.name: tuna
ingredients.notes: sashimi-grade, or trout, or other fatty fish, thinly sliced against the grain (340g)

ingredients.name: avocado
ingredients.notes: cut in half, pitted, peeled, and cut into 8 to 16 slices

steps: Place the leeks in a bowl of cold water and separate the rings. Remove any green rings and reserve these for making stock. Transfer the white rings to a dish towel to dry out for at least 15 minutes so that they're completely dry before frying.

Warm the rice bran or safflower oil in a large heavy-bottom saucepan or deep skillet over medium-high heat (oil should be at least 2 inches / 5cm deep) to 350°F / 180°C. You can test the temperature with an instant-read thermometer or by submerging a wooden spoon.

Fry the tortillas one at a time for about 2 minutes each. Use a pair of chopsticks or two forks to hold down the two edges so that the tortilla doesn't curl up. Once golden, remove from the oil and let it drain on a plate lined with a brown paper bag. Let them all cool for at least 15 minutes while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.

Using the same oil, fry the leeks: Decrease the oil temperature slightly to 300°F / 150°C. Drop in the leeks and move them around constantly while they fry so they cook and color evenly. The instant you see the leeks turning golden, remove them with a slotted spoon and set them on the plate to cool completely.

Marinate the fish: Place the fish in a bowl and drizzle it with the olive oil so that the citrus and soy sauce don't bite into the fish and give it a gray cast. After lightly coating the fish with oil, immediately add the soy sauce and orange juice, toss, and let sit for 5 minutes.
Once the tortillas are cool, spread 1 tsp of the chipotle mayonnaise on each one. (Ensure tortillas are cool so the mayonnaise does not melt.)
On top of the mayonnaise, distribute the sliced fish in one layer. Scatter with the fried leeks and top with the avocado.
Just before serving, add a pinch of the finishing salt. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Pescado a la Talla (Contramar’s Signature Red and Green Grilled Red Snapper)

ingredients.name: red snapper
ingredients.notes: whole, butterflied, OR 4 (8 oz / 230g) boneless red snapper fillets, with skin on

ingredients.name: Salsa Roja Asada
ingredients.notes: or another red salsa of your choosing

ingredients.name: Salsa Verde Cruda
ingredients.notes: or another green salsa of your choosing

steps: To make the green sauce: Place the garlic, parsley, oil, cumin, and salt in the jar of a blender and puree until smooth.
Once you are ready to cook your fish, heat a grill to medium or a grill pan over medium heat. Brush the cooking surface with oil so that the fish won’t stick.
Clean your fish well, then pat it dry.
Using a sharp knife, crosshatch the flesh on the diagonal, making cuts about 1/2 inch (12mm) deep and 1 inch (2.5cm) apart.
Sprinkle the fish with salt.

Paint the sauces onto the fish: If using fillets, spread two with 1/2 cup (120ml) of the red sauce each and the other two with 1/2 cup (120ml) of the green sauce. If using a butterflied whole fish, spread the red sauce on one half and the green sauce on the other half. Be careful to coat the entire surface and work the sauce into the crosshatched knife marks.
Grill the fish, skin-side down, until it’s almost cooked through, 7 to 10 minutes.
Using a spatula, carefully flip it over and cook the flesh side until it has char marks and easily releases from the grill or pan.
Place it flesh-side up on a platter or onto individual plates.
Serve with the warm tortillas, a bowl of refried black beans, whatever salsa you wish, and wedges of lime.

title: Seafood Rice with Roasted Tomato & Green Chile # 2

ingredients.name: jalapeño chile
ingredients.notes: fresh (or 4 serranos or 1 habanero or practically any fresh hot chile)

ingredients.name: fish fillet
ingredients.notes: meaty, skinless (mahimahi, halibut, sea bass), cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: mussels
ingredients.notes: big (about 6 ounces) OR about 12 ounces clams

ingredients.name: shrimp
ingredients.notes: medium-large (about 9 ounces), peeled and deveined, if you wish

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.notes: to taste (can range from none to 1.5 tsp)

steps: Heat your broiler.
On a baking sheet, lay out the onion slices, unpeeled garlic and chiles (if using jalapeños, cut them in half lengthwise).
Roast them about 4 inches below the hot broiler for 5 or 6 minutes, until they are blistered and blackened in spots, then flip them over and roast the other side.
Scrape them into a food processor or blender, add the tomatoes (juice and all) and process to a coarse puree.
In a large (4-quart) saucepan, heat the oil over medium-high.
When hot, add the tomato seasoning and stir until the mixture is thick and shiny, about 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for another minute or so, then add the broth and bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce the heat so that the broth very gently simmers and add the fish, mussels (or clams) and epazote (if you have it).
Cover the pot and set the timer for 15 minutes.
When the timer goes off, taste a kernel of rice: If it's still crunchy inside, re-cover the pot and cook a couple of minutes longer.
If it's close to done, add the shrimp, re-cover the pot, turn off the heat and let the shrimp cook gently in the warm, steamy environment for 2 or 3 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro or parsley, then taste and season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and serve with the lime wedges for each person to squeeze on al gusto.

title: Radicchio Trevisano

ingredients.name: aged sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
radicchio Trevisano
ingredients.notes: heads; halved lengthwise through the core

steps: Place the currants in a cup and soak them in warm water and vinegar until soft and plump, about 30 minutes; drain though a fine-mesh sieve.
Preheat a grill or a heavy grill pan over medium-high heat.
Brush the radicchio with olive oil and salt and grill, turning occasionally, until lightly browned and wilted, about 10 minutes.
Toss it in a bowl with vinaigrette and transfer to a plate.
Sprinkle with pine nuts and the currants and crumble goat cheese on top.

title: Via Carota Vinaigrette
steps: Place the shallots in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse with cold water; drain.
Transfer the shallots to a small bowl with the garlic, sugar, and salt.
Strip the thyme leaves off the stems and finely chop the leaves (for about 1 teaspoon thyme); stir into the bowl.
Stir in the vinegar and water.
Pour the olive oil into the bowl in a slow stream, whisking all the while until emulsified.

title: NIKKEI SEA BREAM WITH YUZU & GREEN JALAPEÑO RICE COOKED IN A CLAY POT

ingredients.name: root ginger
ingredients.notes: 2.5cm / 1in piece, peeled and cut into fine julienne strips

steps: Wash the rice in a bowl with plenty of fresh water using a circular motion with your hand. Drain the water and repeat this rinsing three or four times until the water runs clear. Let the rice drain in a colander for at least 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the soaking and cooking broth. Combine the dashi or water, mirin and light soy sauce and set aside. Soak the drained rice in the cooking broth in a donabe or clay pot for 30 minutes.

Tightly wrap a tea-towel (dish towel) over the lid of a Japanese clay pot (known as donabe). After the soaking and before cooking, scatter half of the ginger strips over the rice, lay the sea bream fillets on the top (I like to arrange the fillets to look like an open flower), place the lid on top and bring to the boil.

Once boiling, bring the temperature down to the lowest setting and cook for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat, and without opening the lid (don’t open the lid at any stage of the cooking process), rest for a further 15 minutes.
To make the dressing just put all the dressing ingredients in a bowl and mix together well.

Take the unopened clay pot to the table, open it in front of your guests and, if desired, carefully remove the skin of the fish. Pour the dressing over the fish and rice then using a wide wooden spoon, fluff the rice well, breaking the fish into tiny pieces and mixing it together with the dressing into the rice. Mix thoroughly. If you are using a rice cooker, follow all the above steps but do not take the rice cooker to the table!
To serve, place the rice in individual rice bowls, top with the remaining julienned ginger in the centre of each bowl followed by a sprinkle of sansho pepper and serve immediately.
notes: See also Naoko Takei Moore's Sea Bream Rice (Tai Meshi) recipe
